records.summary: Run the target adapter conformance suite (issue #31)
Enumerate the adapter package discovery sources without running anything (issue #32). Auto-discovery never installs or trusts
Show one installed package's manifest projection, trust, and provenance (issue #32)
Install one adapter package from a closed source (issue #32).
List the installed adapter packages from the local store inventory (issue #32)
Report or purge the quarantine custody (issue #32)
List the quarantined packages
Purge quarantined bytes (the only removal path)
Release a quarantined package: re-plan it as a normal (trusted) install into the live store under explicit confirmation
Record a revocation for an adapter id/version in the local store (issue #32)
Repoint the selected pin to a previously installed immutable version (issue #32). Bytes are never modified
Run the conformance battery against one adapter executable.
Record an explicit trust transition for an installed package (issue #32)
Update one installed package to another immutable version (issue #32). The plan renders the permission/capability diff; a widening diff refuses without `--allow-escalation`
Optional evidence-bound AI readability analysis
Resolve and assess opt-in architecture policy over declared core evidence
Assess selected modules; source remains read-only and advisory without --check
Emit the versioned language-neutral rule catalog and its coverage boundaries
Compare two admitted profile documents, independently of Model changes
Emit a dedicated architecture lock sidecar for explicit caller persistence
Resolve an exact named profile, parent chain and effective rule digest
List, propose, confirm, and audit the binding registry (issue #42). The core owns every decision; this binary only selects, renders, and maps exits
Re-fingerprint every binding after source changes: a changed signature or path is stale (gate failure) or correctly re-resolved, never silent
Confirm inferred bindings: one by proposal id (with --candidate for an ambiguous proposal), or the unambiguous set as a batch with the planned-and-confirmed preview
Project the whole registry: implement/expose/verify rows with source, confidence, provenance, and freshness
Derive the current confirmation proposals with their full candidate sets; ambiguous mappings list every candidate and pick none
The `cache` subcommands: the thin status/clear handoff (issue #20)
Clear the cache home (`.lekalo/cache/**` except migration state)
Print the read-only, bounded cache health projection
Validate or inspect one data-classification attachment against the project (issue #87): custody, subject resolution, grants, and the governing policy
Inspect one classification attachment: the resolved kinds of every declared subject in canonical order

Validate one classification attachment and its governing policy against the project: custody pins, subject resolution, grant coherence, and (under the strict profile) the sensitive-sink rule over the declared graph. The documents are read from the given project-relative paths; the core owns every decision
Print the embedded contract version registry

Build a bounded context capsule for one semantic symbol, or for the explicitly supplied changed symbols. The human projection of the valid result is the agent-facing Markdown; `--json` emits the structured capsule (`lekalo/context/v1.0.0`)

Report the context-budget and local-understandability metrics of one symbol, one module, or the whole project (issue #75): the measured dependency closure before any budget selection, the required semantic facts separated from supporting facts and optional source, cross-module hops, the explainable over-budget breakdown, advisory extraction boundaries, and the opt-in capsule simulation. Advisory by default; a mandatory `--policy` document is the only denied path. No default budget exists: an explicit `--budget` or `--budget-profile` is required

Record, verify, and govern AI-written implementation in contracted mode (issue #40). The model is primary, the target source is maintained code, and the adapter checks conformance and may generate support artifacts only. The core owns every decision; this binary only selects, renders, and maps exits
Attach verbatim native-test or gate ids to one recorded symbol
Run the conformance gate: re-fingerprint every binding, recompute the canonical signatures and declared effects from the typed IR, and re-digest every fingerprinted support artifact
Register one support artifact in the ownership manifest; the path must stay inside the generated home, and maintained implementation paths refuse by construction
Merge one adapter declaration document into the conformed registry; a binding recorded with a fingerprint is conformance evidence until the source or the contract changes

Report semantic coupling and change-radius metrics with graph evidence for one symbol, one module, the whole project, or typed changed inputs (issue #77). Separate public contracts from internal impact and expose cycles, shared state, and configurable threshold/baseline findings. Advisory by default; an explicitly selected strict coupling profile may deny. Use `--context-budget` to include the optional context plan
Derive or inspect the data-flow report over the classified project (issue #87): flows, tenant relations, gate decisions, and the first-class unknown list

Derive the data-flow report over the classified project: flows, findings, unknowns, and the aggregated gate verdict, pinned to the exact input digests. Read-only; the report is never written by this command
Compare two accepted project selections semantically
Diagnose project, model, adapters, artifacts, and integrations in one read-only readiness report
Project the declared and detected effect graph of operations
Classify parallel-change conflicts for one explicit change set.
Show one operation's declared and detected effects
Report which operations write (or read with `--readers`) one resource or exact field
Validate preregistered Framework Lift protocols and compare local recorded evidence. Never launches an agent/provider or exports private artifacts (issue #100)
Compare all scheduled slots; retains missing, failed and retried attempts
Verify approved protocol pins and baseline file bytes before an executor call
Admit one recorded arm against its exact preregistration (no execution)
Validate one closed local evaluation document; does not attest execution
Validate, evaluate, render, or compare typed-expression attachments (issue #66). The core owns every decision; this binary only selects, renders, and maps exits
Compare two same-family attachments and classify every changed path; the verdict stays data, never an exit code
Evaluate the shared vectors of one attachment against the deterministic reference evaluator with the injected clock
Render one complete cross-target program (node, php, or go) that computes the shared vectors
Validate one attachment: exhaustive static typing, canonical bytes, and the required capability set
Check generated-artifact ownership and drift, or plan and apply a confirmed clean of orphaned generated files
Project the deterministic dependency graph of semantic symbols
Report what depends on one symbol (the reverse view)
Export the whole canonical graph as compact deterministic JSON
Report the shortest dependency path between two symbols
Show one symbol with its direct dependencies and dependents

Record, inspect, and retain the local-only run history and metrics recorder (issue #121). Fully offline, repository/tenant isolated under `.lekalo/history/`, atomic with recovery, and with no export surface: public payloads are built only by the aggregate consumer, never here
Clear one whole scope through the same transactional delete/invalidation path
Compact the store with `VACUUM` after deletes have committed; a failure is reported separately and never undoes a deletion
Delete one raw record; deletion transactionally invalidates every dependent index/claim reference
The typed local dependent-reference seam for the evidence consumers (indexes, claims, aggregate inputs)
Bind one local dependent reference to live source records; a registration that would create a dependency cycle refuses
Live revalidation of one dependent reference: every bound digest must resolve to live same-scope bytes right now
Create the governed history home (`.lekalo/history/`) with its generated ignore protection and verified untracked custody
The bounded, sorted, same-scope-only list page
Enforce retention for one scope; dry-run lists the victims, `--apply` deletes them with dependent invalidation atomically

Validate and atomically append one bounded typed harness observation from stdin (`--input -`). The recorder exit proves ingestion only: a recorded operation whose own status is `fail` still ingests validly
Verify integrity, foreign keys, identity, and every record digest, then rebuild the secondary index from validated surviving records only
Configure the store-wide retention bounds; the strictest applicable bound is enforced per tenant scope
Mint one random local tenant scope token. No tenant name or host identity is accepted or derivable
Mint one random local tenant scope token
Show one sanitized record and its separately stored assertion set, named apart for the local operator
Report the impact and change radius of one semantic symbol, or of the changed inputs of a Git revision range or the working tree
Bootstrap a new greenfield Lekalo project in the invocation directory (issue #97), or adopt an existing repository with `--adopt` (issue #38)
Inspect one semantic symbol: identity, contract, effects, relations, and bounded projections in one deterministic view
Load YAML/JSON sources, resolve imports, and emit the canonical model
Create the committed project lock, or check an existing one
Privacy-safe public metrics from versioned local run history
Preview or confirm a privacy-safe aggregate from live local history
Recheck source deletion, byte integrity and current declared authorization
Migrate the Model contract version to a registered target, or roll back one recorded migration
Create one additional empty module in an initialized project (issue #97)
Create one additional empty module: the module manifest and nothing else, no-overwrite, gated by the normal load and validation path

Plan native build/test gates over a Node workspace (issue #48). Planning is read-only: it produces the immutable proposed plan with its digest. Execution of trusted synthetic fixtures is owned by the test-only harness — the production binary never launches a gate command and answers with a typed refusal

Propose the immutable native gate plan over the current workspace: workspace inventory, affected closure, confirmed commands, and the plan digest. Read-only; never launches a command. The plan document is read from stdin

Resolve NFR constraints against their measured evidence (issue #85): the gate, the derived report, and the closed queries. The core owns every decision; this binary only selects, renders, and maps exits
Compare two same-family NFR attachments semantically; the verdict stays data (breaking, non-breaking, policy-change)

Project the impact of a constraint change through the accepted impact engine: the changed constraints' scope symbols enter as a synthesized typed changed-input set, and the standard impact payload carries the affected scenarios and gates
Run one closed query over the resolution report
Emit the canonical resolution report: per-constraint statuses, per-environment rows, foreign evidence, open questions, and the gate verdict
Emit the neutral #22 trace-manifest projection of the resolved NFR constraints: constraint, symbol, and gate nodes, the implements and evidences edges, and the explicit gaps

Validate the attachment and gate every mandatory constraint: violated, unverified, stale, unsupported, or conflicted mandatory rows deny the gate; `--strict` escalates advisory violated/unverified/stale rows into the denied set
Record, bind, verify, and promote existing code in observed mode (issue #39). The core owns every decision; this binary only selects, renders, and maps exits
Attach native tests and gates to one recorded symbol

Record the deterministic baseline metrics document over the current observed index (issue #49): the index digest, the binding-state counts, the scan identity, and — when a plan document is supplied — the validated identity of the confirmed native gate plan (the production surface never launches it). Deterministic: an identical index and plan identity write byte-identical documents
Bind one recorded symbol to a source location explicitly
Run the staleness gate over every recorded binding; any stale binding fails with registered diagnostics
Confirm one inferred binding; confirmed facts are user-owned
Project the observed impact of one recorded symbol; the recorded graph always reports its own incompleteness
Project the observed card of one recorded symbol
Plan (with --dry-run) or apply (with --confirm) the explicit promotion of observed symbols into the canonical model
Merge one adapter scan document into the observed index; a binding recorded under a stable key survives a source move
Render, check, or inspect the OpenAPI projection of one transport attachment (issue #46). The core owns every decision; this binary only reads the documents, selects, renders, and maps exits
Check a maintained OpenAPI document against the current attachment: bind every operation, recompute the fragments, and report per-pointer drift plus the unbound-manual inventory
Compare two same-family attachments and report the pointer-level view of the transport compatibility classes; the verdict stays data, never an exit code
Inspect one endpoint's rendered operation: the joined Model surface plus every projected OpenAPI member
Render the OpenAPI document of one validated attachment: the canonical bytes, their digest, and the projection findings

The privacy family (issue #119): the deterministic, custody- verified export-decision evaluator over the frozen #120 policy. The core owns every decision; this binary only reads the decision file, renders, and maps exits

Evaluate one export-decision input (exact JSON bytes) against the custody-verified frozen #120 policy. Prints the closed `ExportDecisionOutput` and exits 0 (allow), 3 (deny or transform-required), or 1 (malformed input or custody failure). Startup, parse, and custody failures print the separate closed CLI error object on stderr

Export one artifact document under the fail-closed privacy pipeline (issue #119): class resolution, decision evaluation, the closed redaction transforms, the leak-scanner verification pass, and the writes under `.lekalo/privacy/`. `--dry-run` prints the exact candidate payload and the redaction diff and writes nothing
Show the redaction diff contract of one payload document (issue #119): the closed transforms, the leak findings, and the redacted payload on stdout. Read-only: writes nothing

Print the canonical `{subjectDigest, subjectProfileRef}` of the synthesized decision input for one artifact + destination (issue #119, fix round 2, C-F1): the pair an operator needs to author authorizing evidence. Metadata-only; the evidence positions are excluded from the projection, so authoring never needs a fixpoint. Exit contract like `export`'s pre-evaluation failures

Emit the issue #34 workflow-provider discovery manifest for AIFHub `/aif-*` consumers: a closed, deterministic receipt that works outside any project, reads nothing, launches nothing, and writes nothing
Emit the workflow-provider manifest (capability discovery)
Validate one declarative query-model attachment against the project, or compare two attachments of the same family
Compare two same-family attachments and classify every changed path; the verdict stays data, never an exit code
Validate the attachment against the selected project and emit the deterministic plan summary of every declared query
Report phase readiness with required and optional checks
Resolve one requirements attachment against its project: the read-only OpenSpec requirement traceability integration
Run one closed query over the resolution report
Emit the canonical resolution report: catalog, coverage gaps, conflicts, and changed-requirement impact
Emit the neutral #22 trace-manifest projection of the resolved requirements
Validate the attachment and gate every requirement reference: stale, missing, or conflicted references deny the gate
Scan existing code through one target adapter and record the bindings (issue #42). Everything after the program path is passed to the adapter verbatim (no shell), so adapter flags come last
Report the freshness panel — lock, cache, bindings, artifacts — plus the exact git/model/lock revisions

The storage family: the engine matrix, profile validation, the deterministic DDL rendering, migration planning, drift, and capability mapping (issue #69), plus the storage-projection validate/project/diff/introspect-check/plan handoff (issue #117). The core owns every decision; this binary only reads documents, selects, renders, and maps exits
Project the engine capability snapshot, optionally mapped against one transaction-concurrency attachment's requirements

Run the storage-component conformance battery over the committed fixture set: the profile and its bound projection, the optional checked-mode evidence pair, the engine input document, and the runtime goldens. A skip is never a pass
Render the deterministic DDL document of one profile over its bound storage-projection attachment
Compare two same-family attachments and classify every changed path; the verdict stays data, never an exit code
Compare one checked-mode storage-observation evidence document against its bound storage-projection attachment and report the typed drift findings
Print the single runtime-neutral engine input document every runtime consumer (Node.js, Laravel, Go, Rust) receives
Compare one declared projection against one adapter-produced introspection evidence document; drift is data, never a guessed repair. No database connection exists anywhere

Derive the bounded Laravel migration input from two same-project storage-projection attachments under one engine profile (issue #57). The plan is gated by the effective policy — destructive **or** backfill obligations block — and the blocked input prints with its planId for --confirm. A validated rename-history document turns same-entity physical renames into RENAME steps instead of drop+add. The output is a dry run: artifacts are never written and no database is contacted

Derive the deterministic migration plan from two same-project storage-projection attachments under one engine profile. A destructive plan is gated: it prints blocked unless the exact planId is named with --confirm (the native-gate custody pattern)

Derive the non-executable migration plan over one comparison; destructive and backfill steps carry the explicit gate. The plan-id acknowledgment stays data: with `--confirm` and the exact plan identity the envelope records the acknowledgment, and a wrong identity refuses as stale
Print the owner-published engine version matrix, or one version's capability answers
Derive one namespace's storage projection from one attachment and emit its canonical bytes
Validate one storage-projection attachment against the selected project and emit the derived-projection summary of every declared namespace
Validate one storage-engine attachment and emit its canonical bytes
Validate, project, or compare storage-engine-profile capability evidence (issue #117)
Emit the capability snapshot JSON of one profile (the #24 bridge input)
Compare two same-family profiles and classify every changed path; the verdict stays data, never an exit code
Compare two profiles and emit the portability report
Validate one engine profile attachment and emit the identity summary
Validate, canonically export, or query one neutral trace manifest
Assess an explicit neutral mapping and revision-bound provider receipts

Rebuild the scenario → test → gate manifest from the adjudicated run-record ingest home and persist the canonical document under `.lekalo/import/trace/`. The one write command of the trace surface: exactly one derived document, atomically replaced
Emit the canonical bytes and digest of one validated manifest
Run one closed forward/reverse query over a validated manifest
Validate one neutral trace manifest document
Validate, inspect, project or compare HTTP/JSON transport attachments (issue #70). The core owns every decision; this binary only selects, renders, and maps exits
Compare two same-family attachments and classify every changed path; the verdict stays data, never an exit code
Inspect one endpoint binding: the joined Model surface (method, path, invokes) plus every declared transport member
Project the attachment into the canonical route surface of one closed namespace (node, laravel, go, or rust)
Validate the attachment against the selected project: wire normalization, custody, the semantic pass, and — under `--strict` — the mapping-completeness and capability gates
Preview a deterministic lock update, or apply one exact plan
Validate the semantic layer of a Lekalo project over the typed IR
Run the read-only verification pipeline over a validated project: core validation, drift, per-target adapter validation, portable
